newsitem.title: USA: Local manufacturing activity robust - Richmond Fed.
newsitem.headline: Local manufacturing activity robust - Richmond Fed.

text.p: Manufacturing activity in the fifth U.S. economic region was robust and exceeded forecasts in March, a Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond economist said.
"March was a month of very strong growth here," Raymond Owens, economist at the Richmond Fed, said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"Some of them were seasonal in nature; we expected to have a rebound in March but certainly the magnitudes of growth we saw have exceeded the rebound of past years by a good margin," he added.
Owens comments followed the release on Tuesday of the Richmond Fed manufacturing survey for March, which showed, among other things, that new orders rose to 25 from a minus one reading in February.
The Richmond Fed economist said regional sales strength was broad-based, adding that local consumers appear to be confident in the economy.

"Sales strength was broad-based. It was both in big ticket and smaller ticket items. It also suggests ... a consumer that feels very confident about income and about employment prospects," Owens said.

The economist also said regional price expectations were seen remaining stable, adding that he felt there are "expectations that prices aren't going to change a great deal over (a six-month) horizon."
